questions.question: In the BLIMP method, what operation is applied to each seismic trace at step 3?
required_facts: Step 3 applies a band-limited integration filter to each seismic trace and exponentiates the result.
questions.manual_evidence_note: 1996-21.pdf physical p3, BLIMP step 3; chunk _10 contains both clauses. Filters match paper/en/document ID.

questions.question: For the Nebraska canal CSP system, what frequency sweep and repetition rate were used?
required_facts: The signal swept from 2 to 10 kHz at 4 times per second.
questions.manual_evidence_note: fs11503.pdf physical p4 states both facts; chunk _23 contains both. Manifest type technical_report (not report), language en.

questions.question: What sound velocity was assumed through the water column and unconsolidated saturated sediments?
required_facts: The assumed sound velocity was 5,000 feet per second (5,000 ft/s).
questions.manual_evidence_note: fs11503.pdf physical p6 assigns 5,000 ft/s to both media; chunk _36 contains the sentence. Filters match manifest metadata.

questions.question: In the St. Louis example, what geophone frequency and spacing were used?
required_facts: The St. Louis data used 4.5-Hz horizontal geophones spaced at 1.5 m.
questions.manual_evidence_note: s10950-021-10042-z.pdf physical p15, St. Louis subsection states 4.5-Hz horizontal geophones at 1.5-m spacing; chunk _107 contains it. Filters match manifest.

questions.question: When are intercept-time formulas preferred over crossover-distance formulas, and when is the reverse preference stated?
required_facts: Intercept-time formulas are preferred when plotting control for V2 is better than for V1.
Crossover-distance formulas are preferred when plotting control for V1 is better than for V2.
questions.manual_evidence_note: twri_2-d2.pdf physical p21 and figure text; both conditional recommendations span chunks _125/_126. Filters match textbook/en manifest metadata.

questions.question: In the textbook's worked two-layer example, how do the single-shot nonreversed and reversed dipping-boundary interpretations differ in layer geometry, depth, and velocity?
required_facts: The single-shot nonreversed interpretation gives a horizontal second layer 21 ft deep with velocity 10,600 ft/s.
The reversed dipping-boundary interpretation gives an 8.7-degree dip and velocity 15,000 ft/s, with interface depth 20 ft at the updip shotpoint and 120 ft at the downdip shotpoint.
questions.manual_evidence_note: twri_2-d2.pdf physical p22 contains the two numbered cases. Production chunk text has joined forms 'Summary ofexampleproblem', 'nonreversedseismic-refraction', 'interpretationgives'; evidence spans adjacent chunks _128/_129. Filters match manifest.
